chunks: Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, and Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sahban, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them.

He said: Indeed, an Arabian came to Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his Family), and he went out to him wearing a red-dyed robe. He said: O Muhammad, you have come out to me as if you are a young man. He (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Yes, O Arabian, I am the Young Man, the son of the Young Man, the brother of the Young Man. He said: O Muhammad, as for the Young Man, then yes. But how (are you) the son of the Young Man and the brother of the Young Man?

So he said: Have you not heard Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, saying: 'They said: We heard a young man mentioning them, who is called Ibrahim'? So I am the son of Ibrahim. And as for the brother of the Young Man, indeed a caller cried from Heaven on the Day of Uhud: 'There is no sword but Dhu'l-Faqar, and there is no Young Man but Ali.' Ali is my brother and I am his brother.

key_terms.الْفَتَى: The Young Man (a title of youth and vigor)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Prophet's statement 'I am the Young Man, son of the Young Man, brother of the Young Man'?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* elucidates the Prophet's tripartite title by linking 'son of the Young Man' to Prophet Ibrahim (citing Surah Al-Anbiya) and 'brother of the Young Man' to Ali ibn Abi Talib via the celestial proclamation on the Day of Uhud. It highlights the Shia theological emphasis on Ali’s unique status as the ultimate *Fatā* (young man/hero) and the Prophet’s spiritual lineage, reinforcing the concept of *Nubuwwah* and *Imamah* through Quranic exegesis and historical event (*Hadith al-Uhud*).
